findings.reason: the plan must either relocate `VesselShell`/`extract_vessel_shells` to a neutral module or state why the 2D core may depend on the 3D subpackage.
findings.text: §1 types the core `MachineGeometry` field with `VesselShell` and has `extract_geometry` call `extract_vessel_shells`, both owned by `imas_ink/three_d/walls.py`; `imas_ink/__init__.py:7` documents that `imas_ink.three_d` "is also not eagerly imported", yet importing `imas_ink.three_d.walls` pulls the whole 3D subpackage (verified: `import imas_ink.extract, imas_ink.figures` leaves `imas_ink.three_d` out of `sys.modules`, while `import imas_ink.three_d.walls` loads it) — the reuse inverts the core→3D boundary the package maintains.

findings.reason: the plan should state which series owns the axes label/legend or make label emission explicit for the multi-series case.
findings.text: §3 lets a panel be a list of `TimeSeries` "drawn on the same axes through render_mpl", but the loop at `figures.py:88` calls `render_mpl` once per panel and `_render_timeseries_mpl` (`imas_ink/mpl.py:537`) sets the y-axis label and legend on every call, so drawing two series on one axes silently overwrites the label with the second series' and the done-when (asserts lines/dash/colour only) never exercises labelling; the interface hides the conflict instead of resolving it.

findings.reason: the sections must fix or drop the conditional constant and justify trace_color as a distinct name rather than reusing wall_color.
findings.text: §1 says "A new InkStyle constant is added only if the vessel needs a weight distinct from the wall", leaving a public-definition addition indeterminate inside a section declared `implementable`; §3 at line 134 adds `InkStyle.trace_color` defined as "the ink black the wall uses", i.e. the existing `wall_color = "#000000"` (`imas_ink/style.py:47`), a duplicate value rather than a merge; against a supplied budget of 0 in all four families the plan nets ~5 new public names and retires none, and §1's conditional constant cannot be accounted for in the section's own text.

deep_module-1.reason: plan v5 §3: the first series owns the panel's y-label, units and time label; later series draw lines only in the first's colour with no label or legend; the done-when asserts the label and the absence of a legend

interface_budget-1.reason: plan v5 settles both: §1 adds no style constant (the vessel uses wall_color and wall_linewidth) and §3 drops trace_color, keeping only trace_linestyle with its retirement accounting

reuse_search-1.reason: plan v5 §1 moves WallOutline2D, VesselShell and extract_vessel_shells into core imas_ink/geometry.py, three_d/walls.py imports them, and the done-when asserts imas_ink.three_d stays out of sys.modules

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — no new module is added, but the new "panel is one TimeSeries or a list" interface on `time_trace_figure_mpl` hides an unresolved label/axis-label/legend conflict between two `render_mpl` calls on one axes.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: pass — the plan extends the single vessel extractor (`three_d/walls.py`) and the single 2D wall component (`components.py`) and names both `WallOutline(...)` construction sites (`figures.py:181`, `figures.py:702`); it forks no shared mechanism.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; the plan adds ~5 new public names across three sections (MachineGeometry.vessel_shells, WallOutline.vessel_shells, InkStyle.wall_linestyle, InkStyle.trace_color, InkStyle.trace_linestyle) plus two new kwargs, and while each section says it "retires nothing", §1 leaves one InkStyle constant conditional and unresolved, and §3's trace_color simply restates the existing wall_color value rather than merging with it.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan does search the owning module and extends `extract_vessel_shells` (`imas_ink/three_d/walls.py:151`), `_select_description_2d` (`imas_ink/extract.py:322`) and `WallOutline` (`imas_ink/components.py:138`), but it reuses `VesselShell` from a subpackage the core deliberately keeps out of its eager import graph without addressing the layering cost.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — every change is a parameter or field on an existing owner (`geometry_figure_mpl`, `_render_wall_mpl`, `_render_wall_alt`, `_render_timeseries_mpl/_alt`, `MachineGeometry`, `WallOutline`), not a new layer over one.
